sectionSubtitle: You've led teams, shipped products, and made millions for your company. But the interview room is a different battlefield.

painPoints.title: You're Solving at the Wrong Level
painPoints.description: Directors and VPs are expected to drive architecture decisions, not implement them. Yet most candidates dive into low-level details because that's what made them successful as engineers.
painPoints.statLabel: of senior leaders fail SD interviews

painPoints.title: No Executive Communication Framework
painPoints.description: Interviewers want to see you think like a leader: stakeholder alignment, trade-off analysis, risk mitigation. Most candidates ramble instead of leading the conversation.

painPoints.title: Imposter Syndrome Kicks In
painPoints.description: After years of managing, you haven't coded or whiteboarded in ages. The pressure of 'proving yourself' again makes even seasoned leaders freeze.

painPoints.title: Wrong Preparation Materials
painPoints.description: YouTube tutorials and LeetCode are designed for engineers. There's almost no content for Director/VP-level system design interviews. You're studying the wrong playbook.

systemDesignDifference.title: System Design for Leaders is NOT the Same
systemDesignDifference.subtitle: What got you here won't get you there

comparison.leader: Business impact, organizational buy-in, multi-year roadmaps
Time-to-market vs. technical debt vs. team capacity

systemDesignDifference.callout: I've conducted 100+ interviews at Amazon. The rubric for Staff+, Director, and VP candidates is fundamentally different. Most coaches don't know this because they've never been on the hiring committee for these roles.

solution.title: I Teach Leaders to Interview Like Leaders
points: Executive-level system design frameworks used by actual FAANG hiring committees
Bar-raiser perspective on what separates 'hire' from 'strong hire'
Real mock interviews with the intensity of actual loops
Personalized feedback on your leadership signals, not just technical accuracy
